side_a: CC 1.16.5: Appointment, rotation, recusal, and appeals are external to this system’s control and follow explicit anti-capture rules.
side_b: CC 4.3: A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else;
note: Who answers an agent's deferral: Wise Authorities appointed under the Annex B charter, outside the system (CC 1.16.5, CC 1.9 'designated'), or whoever the agent's steward seated by a delegates_to, and the steward itself where no seat row exists (CC 4.3). CC 4.3 says 'the charter governs the designated body' and does not say how that body relates to a conferred seat. The CC 4.5.1 register also records 'none' as the exit from the WA relation, while CC 4.3 lets the conferrer end a seat by withdraws. CC 4.3 is the normative, wire-checked rule.

side_a: CC 6.1.5 "(governed by LRU-only): no holding claim, no compress request, no rarest-first biasing"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "hides who published a federation-scope item from the nodes that store it, from the directory, and, with shaping, from an observer of the network"
note: 'Anonymous tier' names two things. In CC 6.1.5 (SR-2), 6.1.5.3, 6.1 (WW-2) and 6.1.8 (RB-1) it is a class of content with no holding claim, outside the witness and exempt from anti-entropy; in CC 5.4.6 it is an onion transport for federation-scope items that are stored and listed in the directory. Whether an item published through the tier carries holding claims and is replicated differs by which section is read.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: A producer MUST NOT ship a dimension family this Part does not register.
side_b: CC 3.1.7: The ProducerSteward fallback remains only for the open-vocabulary space this Part deliberately leaves open.
note: One sentence forbids shipping any unregistered family and a neighbour orders a substrate to fail emission on a family with no registry row (namespace_family_unregistered); two others keep an admissible open vocabulary and the x_private range. A reader of the first refuses a party's own unregistered dimension, a reader of the second admits it under the producer-steward fallback. The closing paragraph of CC 3.1.7 (open vocabulary is for a party's own dimensions, never a shipped component's) supports the second, with the MUST NOT bound to shipped components.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.4 **substrate-protective perceptual-hash tripwire at every scope-*widening* promotion event**, never on the device, never inside a private cohort
side_b: CC 3.2 runs on the post exactly as it runs on a promotion into the Commons — never inside a private cohort, never on the device
note: A widening from self to family, or from family to a gated community, is a scope-widening promotion that lands inside a private cohort. "Every widening" (CC 3.1.3.4: "Every widening is an act on specific bytes ... each with its own emission and tripwire") matches it; "never inside a private cohort" and the next sentence of 1.13.3.4 (only a promotion into the Commons or a post into a public room is matched) do not. The Commons-or-public-room reading is the one the privacy position supports.

side_a: CC 4.5.3: A duty-holder's notice is admitted by the [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5) enforced-admission rule and reaches the bytes plane only.
side_b: CC 7.5.5: a lawful order to destroy sealed material is a `takedown_notice:court_order:v1` executed as the tombstone by digest of [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) with every purge guarantee
note: A court_order notice is a duty-holder basis (immediate-removal, bytes plane only, destroyed on receipt); CC 7.5.5 has it destroy a sealed retirement record (identity record, audit trail, logs: rows on other planes) with 'every purge guarantee', which in CC 4.5.3 belongs to the root-cosigned steward_purge (any plane, 72 h dwell, whole or not at all). Which reach and which dwell a court order has differs by section.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.2: if now > deadline and completion is None:
side_b: manifests/reactions.json consent:deletion_sla:{days}: the breach reaction at the close of the sla clock is emitted unless the target was withdrawn, superseded or purged; consent:deletion_complete is not among the conditions
note: The data follows CC 3.3.1 D1 (the row's absence), not the CC 4.4.3.5.2 watcher (the producer's deletion_complete). The same data row starts the clock on 'withdrawn of target' and excuses the breach on 'withdrawn of target', so as written a subject's withdrawal both starts and clears the watch; the text's D1 means the producer's own composer.

side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.6: `consent:state:granted` + envelope `valid_until = asserted_at + 14d` + auto-renew dimension on interaction (consumer-policy concern)
note: A temporary grant lapses 14 days after it was granted under CC 3.3.1 and 14 days after the last interaction under CC 4.4.3.5.6, which adds an auto-renew the first does not state; who signs the renewal is not said, and a grant row is the subject's to sign (CC 3.3.1 Emitted by). CC 3.4.13 and CC 3.4.12 forbid auto-renew for their own grants.

side_a: CC 5.2: or each `member.key_id` in the named family's roster (family).
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: At every sealed write the substrate wraps the content's DEK to every current recipient occurrence and emits one `key_grant` row per wrap.
note: CC 5.2 wraps a family write once per member key and names the wrap target by key id; CC 4.4.3.4.1 (the cascade's home) wraps to every occurrence of every recipient, and CC 5.2's own next paragraph says the target is the occurrence's encryption_pubkeys, never a signing key. Under the first a family member's second device reads nothing. The home supports per occurrence.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "`authority_id` names a key: a `federation_keys.key_id`, or an organisation"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8 "Its own walk from its own edges reaches the issuing authority for the row's class, and that authority's charter declares the class."
note: CC 2.4.1.2.1 and CC 4.4.3.4.3 let anyone be a licence authority under a bare key; CC 4.4.3.8 honours a licence only where the authority's charter declares the class, and CC 4.4.3.2.8 carries that declaration on a signed community record. A bare key has no charter, so its licences are honoured by no reader under 4.4.3.8 and folded as licensure under 2.4.1.2.1. The CC 4.3 seat rule ('holds a live licence from that authority') does not say which reading it takes.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: So a node whose owner resolves to the `minor` band MUST NOT carry a federation-scope owner-binding, and admission MUST refuse the promotion.
side_b: CC 4.5.13: **Announcing starts on,** its cost on screen.
note: With no assurance on record an owner resolves to under_13, which implies minor (CC 3.4.13), so admission refuses the federation-scope binding for every person who has not yet shown a provider-rung signal; CC 4.5.13 has announcing on by default 'for nearly everyone'. Whether 'resolves to the minor band' means attested as a minor, or includes the fail-secure default, is unstated and decides who is reachable.

side_a: CC 2.4 "A `dimension` on **any** of the five MUST resolve through the namespace exactly as it does on `scores`"
side_b: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
note: The same finding as under row_shape, seen from the gate: CC 2.4 has the admitting substrate resolve every dimension; CC 2.1's member table says the substrate does not parse it.

side_b: data: manifests/namespace_registry.json: content_rating:{scheme}:{rating} has reserved false and no reserved_rule
note: CC 4.4.3.8 and CC 3.2 treat content_rating:* as a reserved prefix whose emitter role is conferred by delegation, and CC 3.4.7 has a substrate reject a reserved-prefix row from any other key. The registry, which CC 3.1.7 makes the enforcement surface, carries the family unreserved, so a matcher built from it admits a rating from any key. The CC 3.1.9.2 catalogue row speaks of 'the trusted-publisher emitter rule' and CC 3.4 lists no such reservation.

side_a: CC 2.1 "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
note: CC 2.1 has every scores row at family, community or affiliations name its own producer in attested_key_id and refuses a third party; a key grant is a scores row placed at the content's scope whose attested_key_id is the recipient and whose signer is the sealer (CC 3.1.3, 3.3.2), and group:roster names the group there. CC 2.1 states no exception; the family model records one.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "their **agent** (the agent's local key) are two occurrences of one user identity that share one **Self DEK**"
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "An agent signs no item of a person's queue: the person's choices are the person's."
note: CC 3.3.6.3 defines the roster as the identity_occurrence rows under the fedID and lets "any live roster key" sign as the fedID for every owner act (consent, owner-binding, root acceptance, approving a device), and CC 4.5.13 counts a vote signed by any key of the fedID. If the agent's key is an occurrence of the user, it signs all of these. CC 4.5.13, CC 4.3 and CC 3.3.6.3 ("an agent's occurrence is single-signer") deny it. The denial is the later text and the one CC 1.13.2 supports.

side_a: CC 2.4.1 "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: CC 3.2 "a new guardian's `delegates_to` carried as a `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) replaces the prior binding"
note: CC 2.4.1 confines supersedes to the prior row's own attester, and CC 3.5.1 rule 4 evaluates another attester's composer as a separate chain; CC 3.2 has a new guardian, a different signer, supersede the old guardian's binding. Whether a guardian can be displaced by the incoming guardian's row alone differs. CC 3.2 also writes one row as two types (a delegates_to 'carried as' a supersedes) against the closed type slot of CC 2.4.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.5: "There is no relay tree; the small-group realtime profile of [CC 5.3.3.2](#5.3.3.2) pushes on direct links"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.4: "A member MAY take each layer of a stream from a different parent of the member relay tree"
note: E2, E1 sentence 1, the CC 5.3.3.2 profile table and CC 2.1 deny any media relay role in realtime delivery; CC 5.3.3.4, 5.3.3.2.3 (member relay verifies and forwards chunks) and 5.4.6 (the tree's relays) build one. One implementer ships direct links only, the other a forwarding tree. The later-written sections (binding, trailer, layered multipath) support the tree.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "a scoped body MAY ride the members' **identity-plane link** on three terms"
side_b: CC 5.4.6: "crosses a forwarder only one that has said yes, a consented contact or, as last resort, a serve seat; a stranger is offered none"
note: The first paragraph lets a room body cross any non-member transport node between two members on three terms, none of them the node's consent; "Who carries what" adds that the forwarder must be a carrier that said yes. Two phones behind NATs with only a stranger between them exchange a room body under one reading and not the other. The later paragraph and CC 5.4.3 support the consent condition.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is `u64` **big-endian** and monotonic per RNS Link (transit replay guard).
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.5 `link_seq` is a per-`(link, stream)` counter both ends keep and is never carried in the frame
note: The outer nonce is SHA-256(label, link_id, link_seq) with no stream id in it. One counter per link gives distinct nonces across the streams of a link; one counter per (link, stream), each starting at 0, gives two streams on one link the same outer nonce, and a receiver built the other way cannot open. The nonce formula supports per link; the loss-recovery paragraph is written per (link, stream).

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds"
side_b: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
note: The home table gives rule 2 one condition (the kept list) and says a node MUST admit when a line holds. CC 3.2 adds a second condition for one family. Built from CC 2.4.1.1 alone, a node admits a compromised node key's withdrawal of its own owner. CC 3.2 is the specific rule; the home neither states nor cites the gate.
